title: Chen Szu-Yu, Taiwan's four-time Olympian, retires a month after Asian Championships bronze
seo_title: Chen Szu-Yu, Taiwan's four-time Olympian, retires at 33
description: Chen Szu-Yu, who played at four Olympics for Taiwan and reached world No 10, has retired at 33 after leading a young team to Asian Championships bronze.
standfirst: The 33-year-old, who stepped away in 2024 because of years of pain, said October's Asian Championships in Tashkent had been the perfect way to finish.
body: Chen Szu-Yu, who played at four Olympic Games for Taiwan, has retired from table tennis at the age of 33, a month after helping a young women's team to an Asian Championships bronze medal.

She announced her retirement on social media on Monday evening, Taiwan time, saying that the Asian Championships in Tashkent in October had been her last international event. Her post carried a photo of Taiwan's men's and women's teams together on the podium.

"My last international competition... it ended perfectly, with the men's and women's teams on the podium together at the Asian Championships," she wrote (translated from Chinese). She thanked everyone who had helped her through her career.

Chen played at London 2012, Rio 2016, Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024, where she partnered Lin Yun-Ju in the mixed doubles. She reached a career-high world ranking of 10th in March 2018, and with Lin she won a mixed doubles bronze medal at the 2023 Asian Championships in Pyeongchang.
She represented Taiwan for more than a decade, and her post looked back on 24 years as a player.

Her career nearly ended two years ago. In November 2024, a few months after Paris, she announced that she was stepping away from competition for a while, calling it the hardest decision of her life. She described years of pain that affected her serve and her movement and sometimes kept her awake, and said she had needed injections before and after matches.
"After every match, I hope my hand has not broken," she wrote at the time (translated from Chinese). She asked for time to rest and to find again the player who loved the game.

By 2026 she was back on the tour, playing the World Team Championships in May and a run of WTT Contender and Feeder events through the summer. In July she won the women's doubles title at WTT Feeder Tashkent with Wu Ying Syuan.

At the Asian Championships Chen led a young women's team to the semi-finals, where they lost to Japan, the eventual champions. The bronze was the team's best result for seven years. Taiwan's men also won bronze.

Chen said she finished the championships with a fever, the first time in her life she had had flu, and was relieved that the rest of the team had stayed healthy. Her farewell message was addressed to the players who follow her: "My younger teammates are all great. The future is up to you."
Chen said a longer retirement statement would follow in a while.
